women_problem_title: They run real businesses, but remain invisible to the formal financial system
women_problem_text: Alternative credit scoring models currently used in East Africa rely heavily on mobile money transaction data — leaving out women whose businesses run on cash, and who depend on the trust of their savings group (chama/VICOBA) rather than digital data.
women_model_text: 30–50 women are carefully selected through existing chama/VICOBA groups and agricultural marketing cooperatives (AMCOS).

women_arc.title: Months 1–2: Selection & Baseline Assessment
women_arc.text: Entering through existing group leaders, selecting participants deliberately.

women_arc.title: Months 2–4: Financial Literacy
women_arc.text: Training in daily bookkeeping, costing and pricing, and beginning the NIDA registration process.

women_arc.title: Months 4–8: Formalization Support
women_arc.text: Hands-on help with BRELA registration, TIN, a business license, and a bank account.

women_arc.title: Months 8–11: Loan Readiness
women_arc.text: Women who reach a strong readiness level are connected to partner financial institutions.

women_arc.title: Months 11–12: Evaluation & Outcomes
women_arc.text: Documenting each participant's real outcomes — the evidence base for the next phase.

pilot_text: Biashara Yangu is a digital tool being piloted with our first cohort — one part of a broader BDS service, not the project itself.
policy_items: Tanzania's National Financial Inclusion Framework (2023–2028) has shifted from "access" toward "quality of usage."

Agricultural credit guarantee schemes are helping smallholder farmers access loans — but participating financial institutions still need to identify which farmer is trustworthy. That's where we fit in.
From July 2026, digital payments are legally required for crop sales through AMCOS — directly relevant to our agricultural participants.
women_status_note: We are at an early stage. Real participant numbers will be shown here once available.
youth_problem_text: Computers and internet access in schools are a good start, but without digital safety training, young people are at risk of online scams, harassment, and misuse of their personal information.
youth_status_note: This program is being redesigned from its original "Digital School Club" model — toward direct safety and advancement training, not just device access. Goal: connecting 100+ schools across Tanzania by 2030.
